e101.text: The class bike ride starts in one hour!

e102p.text: Ta-da! My Super-Light Racer! I took off every part that does nothing. Lighter bike, faster bike!

e104b.text: Lightest bike in Singapore. Also the slowest.

e105m.text: Pip! Which parts did you take off?

e106p.text: Only the boring ones. Don't worry, I've got a plan!

e201p.text: Plan one: I pedal harder. Much, much harder!

e202b.text: Plan two: we loop Momo's skipping rope round the gears.

e203m.text: Plan three: put back the chain you took off.

e204p.text: The chain? It just goes round and round, and it makes my socks black!

e205.text: Which fix gets the bike moving? Show me one, two or three fingers!

e206p.text: One! My legs are super strong!

e207b.text: Two. A loop is a loop.

e208m.text: Three. If it was on the bike, maybe it had a job.

e303m.text: The pedals spin, but the back wheel isn't moving!

e304.text: Let's look at that again, in slow motion.

e305.text: The front gear turns, but nothing joins it to the back wheel. Pushing harder on one part cannot do another part's job.

e401.text: Fix two. The skipping rope goes round both gears.

e402b.text: Lift the back wheel, turn the pedal, and watch the magic.

e403m.text: The magic is on your head, Basil.

e501.text: Look closer. Here is the chain from Pip's box of useless parts.

e502m.text: See the gaps in the chain? Each tooth of the gear fits into one, so when the gear turns, it pulls the chain along.

e503.text: The chain pulls the back gear, and the back wheel turns. A smooth rope has no gaps, so the teeth slip.

e504m.text: So the chain has a function. A function is a part's special job. The chain's job is to turn the back wheel when you pedal.

e505b.text: So my rope had no function. Noted.

e601.text: Be one little link of the bike chain! Shrink down. Quietly.

e602.text: You are a link at the top of the chain, between the two gears.

e603.text: Someone pushes the pedals. The front gear's teeth grab you and pull you forward.

e604.text: The whole chain moves with you, and tugs the back gear round. The back wheel turns!

e605.text: Round the front gear you go, back underneath, and round again.

e701.text: Fix three. The chain goes back on.

e702m.text: Lift the back wheel, and turn the pedal...

e703p.text: It spins! The back wheel spins!

e704m.text: Pedals, gear, chain, wheel. Each part acts on the next one.

e705m.text: Scientists say the parts interact: they act on one another.

e706b.text: Even I can't argue with a spinning wheel.

e707b.text: Pip, before you ride, squeeze the brakes.

e708p.text: Squeeze... squeeze... Oh. I took those off too.

e709m.text: Pip! A bike that cannot stop is not safe!

e710.text: The brakes help the bike stop safely, and the bell warns people. Every part has its own function.

e711.text: Quick question! If the bell falls off on the ride, can the bike still move? Think about it.

e712p.text: It can still move, but it is not as safe!

e713.text: Yes! When one part stops working, the whole system is likely to be affected.

e714b.text: So the bike is a system. A system is made up of different parts, and each part has its own special function.

e801.text: With one minute to spare, Pip makes the ride!

e802m.text: Pip, you're puffing! Is something inside you broken too?

e803.text: Nothing is broken. Look closer. Pip's bones and muscles move his legs. His heart beats faster, and he breathes faster.

e805b.text: So Pip's body is made of systems too. Very furry ones.

e807.text: And the ride ends under a giant rain tree.

e808b.text: And a tree is a system too. Its leaves, its stem and its roots each have their own function.

e901.text: Now, here are the words that earn marks.

e903b.text: A system is made up of different parts. Each part has its own function. The parts interact to perform a function. When one part stops working, the whole system is likely to be affected.

e1001p.text: Basil, your tail doesn't pedal, and it doesn't ring. Lighter lizard, faster lizard?

e1002b.text: My tail helps me balance. Every part has a function, Pip.

e1004.text: Picked the chain? You win a point, and so does Momo!

e1102g.text: Excuse me. I'm watered every single day. So why am I wilting?

e1103.text: Next time, at the Plant Help Desk!

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?
